title: Uncertainty quantification in medical AI: why a single confidence score is not enough
subtitle: What aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty mean for patient safety
excerpt: Nearly every clinical AI platform reports a confidence or accuracy metric. Few tell you when their model is uncertain. Understanding uncertainty quantification is the first step toward trusting clinical AI safely.
content:
The gap between confidence and certainty

Nearly every clinical AI platform reports a confidence or accuracy metric. A finding is flagged and accompanied by a number — often between 0 and 1. This score tells you how strongly the model's weights align with the label in its training data. It does not tell you whether the model is certain.

This distinction matters enormously in clinical settings. A model that is 95% confident that a chest X-ray shows a large pleural effusion — and it does — is a reliable result. A model that is 60% confident that a scan shows a small pneumothorax at the lung apex — an area notoriously difficult to read — is a fundamentally different case. Yet both are often presented identically by platforms that report only a confidence score.

Understanding this gap is the first step toward trusting clinical AI safely.
author: Dolapo Ariyo
